name: Chaga mushroom (Inonotus obliquus)
short: Case reports: oxalate kidney damage (oxalate nephropathy) after taking chaga powder by mouth, with dialysis in 2 people and end-stage kidney disease in 1. No trial safety data were found.
text: The evidence of harm comes from case reports of oxalate nephropathy (kidney damage from oxalate crystals) in people who took chaga mushroom powder by mouth. A 72-year-old Japanese woman who had taken chaga powder for 6 months after surgery for liver cancer had declining kidney function, needed haemodialysis, and had oxalate crystals in her kidney biopsy; the authors state that chaga mushrooms contain extremely high oxalate concentrations. A 69-year-old man who had taken chaga powder together with vitamin C for 3 months developed acute kidney injury with nephrotic syndrome and was diagnosed with acute oxalate nephropathy with minimal change disease; he was treated with haemodialysis and high-dose steroids, and his kidney function recovered after 1 month. A 49-year-old Korean man with end-stage kidney disease had chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis with oxalate crystal deposits after long-term chaga powder use for atopic dermatitis; the remaining chaga had an extremely high oxalate content, and the authors call chaga a potential risk factor for chronic kidney disease. No trials reporting adverse events in people were found. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
